key_insight: Selective auditing can reduce expert review while provably keeping the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited below a user-defined threshold.
engineering_relevance: AI pipelines can use confidence scores from a decision model or separate verifier to route proposals between automatic acceptance and expert review.
method: Formulate sequential audit decisions as online constrained optimization.
Minimize auditing frequency subject to a bound on unaudited AI errors.
Derive assumption-free error-control algorithms, including one with asymptotically optimal auditing rates for adversarial and i.i.d. streams.
evidence_signal: Experiments on harmful-request screening, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show valid error control with substantially less human auditing than baselines.
watch_item: Deployment requires reliable expert feedback; asymptotic audit-rate optimality does not imply minimal review effort over short operating periods.
paper_title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
